text: We're using a lot of human driving data to train our deep models. So it's important to make sure that the behavior of the car doesn't seem robotic, it can feel quite unnatural. And from the get-go, we focused on building a fully autonomous system.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny asks about how Waymo creates body language and communication systems for their self-driving cars to interact with other drivers and pedestrians. Shweta explains that Waymo uses human driving data to train their AI models, but filters out bad driving behaviors. She emphasizes that the goal is to make the autonomous vehicle feel natural and trustworthy to riders, not robotic or intimidating, while still being safer than human driving.
text_ko: 우리는 딥러닝 모델(deep models)을 학습시키기 위해 사람들이 운전한 데이터(human driving data)를 많이 활용하고 있어요. 그래서 차량의 행동이 로봇처럼 느껴지면 꽤 어색할 수 있어서, 그런 인상이 들지 않게 하는 게 중요해요. 그리고 처음부터 저희는 완전 자율주행 시스템(fully autonomous system)을 만드는 데 집중해왔어요.
text_zh: 我们用大量的人工驾驶数据 (human driving data) 来训练深度模型 (deep models)。所以很重要的一点是，车辆的行为别显得太机械、像机器人那样——那样会让人觉得很不自然。从一开始我们就把重点放在打造一个完全自动驾驶系统 (fully autonomous system) 上。
text_es: Estamos usando muchos datos de conducción humana para entrenar nuestros modelos de aprendizaje profundo (deep models). Por eso es clave que el comportamiento del vehículo no parezca robótico; puede llegar a sentirse poco natural. Desde el principio nos centramos en desarrollar un sistema totalmente autónomo.
key_sentence: Behavior of the car must feel human-like, not robotic.
original_text: We're using a lot of human driving data to train our deep models. So it's important to make sure that the behavior of the car doesn't seem robotic, it can feel quite unnatural. And from the get-go, we focused on building a fully autonomous system. So it's important to have that familiarity, that trust, building with the riders where they're not daunted by technology, they don't feel like they're sitting in our walk. It has to feel very human-like, but in a good way.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of operating independently without human intervention.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, particularly in robotics and artificial intelligence, 'autonomous' refers to systems that can perform tasks or make decisions without human oversight, enhancing efficiency and scalability.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'autonomous' often conveys a sense of advanced technology, it can also imply a lack of human control, which may raise concerns about safety and ethics.

vocabulary.definition: The manner in which an individual or system acts or conducts itself.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, understanding 'behavior' is crucial for user experience design, as it informs how products should respond to user actions and preferences.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply both intentional actions and automatic responses, so context is important to clarify whether it refers to conscious choices or programmed responses.

vocabulary.definition: Concentrated on a particular task, goal, or area of interest.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, being 'focused' is essential for strategic planning and execution, as it allows teams to allocate resources effectively towards achieving specific objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'focused' implies clarity and determination, it can also suggest a narrow perspective, so it’s important to balance focus with flexibility to adapt to changing circumstances.

text: I would say that the PMC has to be able to go technically indeed, compared to what they would do in other software products. They have to be able to get into the details as much as needed.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny asks about the biggest differences between working at Waymo versus traditional software companies like Amazon or Cisco. Shweta explains that product managers at Waymo need different skills due to the technical complexity of autonomous driving systems. She describes how PMs must dive deeper into technical details and handle more uncertainty than they would in typical software product roles.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 프로젝트 관리 위원회(PMC)는 다른 소프트웨어 제품에서 하던 것과 비교해 확실히 기술적인 부분까지 들어갈 수 있어야 해요. 필요하면 세부사항까지 깊이 파고들 줄 알아야 해요.
text_zh: 我觉得PMC（PMC）在技术上必须能真深入，不能像在其他软件产品里那样走马观花。需要的时候，他们得把技术细节都钻透。
text_es: Diría que el PMC debe poder ir al nivel técnico necesario, en comparación con lo que harían en otros productos de software (software products). Tiene que poder profundizar en los detalles todo lo que haga falta.
key_sentence: They have to be able to get into the details as much as needed.
original_text: I would say that the PMC has to be able to go technically indeed, compared to what they would do in other software products. They have to be able to get into the details as much as needed. They have to be okay with uncertainty and ambiguity. Again, I think, that is part and parcel of any product management role, but it's even more so here.

vocabulary.definition: Specific pieces of information or elements that contribute to a larger picture or understanding of a subject.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, focusing on 'details' is crucial for ensuring accuracy in project execution, product development, and strategic planning, as overlooking them can lead to significant errors.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'details' can imply a level of thoroughness that is necessary for success, but excessive focus on minutiae may be viewed as micromanagement in some contexts.

text: The MVP bar itself for safety is extremely high for us.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny continues asking about differences between Waymo and traditional software companies. Shweta explains how the concept of Minimum Viable Product (MVP) - a core principle in software development where you release a basic version and iterate - works differently at Waymo. Because autonomous vehicles must prioritize safety above all else, their definition of 'minimum viable' still requires an extremely high safety standard, unlike typical software products where you can launch with basic features and improve over time.
text_ko: 안전 측면에서의 MVP 기준(MVP bar)은 저희에게 굉장히 높아요.
text_zh: 就安全这块来说，我们对最小可行产品（MVP）的要求本身就很高。
text_es: El listón de seguridad para el producto mínimo viable (MVP) nos queda extremadamente alto.
key_sentence: The MVP bar itself for safety is extremely high for us.
original_text: The concept of MVP, which is so widely popular in the SaaS product management world or product management world, in general, has a whole new meaning here at Waymo when you work in a product like this because safety is on top of mind for all of us and can't really cut corners on safety. The MVP bar itself for safety is extremely high for us.

vocabulary.definition: The phrase 'extremely high' denotes a level or degree that is significantly above average or standard expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, particularly regarding standards or expectations, 'extremely high' can refer to rigorous benchmarks that must be met for safety, quality, or performance.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys urgency and seriousness, often implying that the stakes are elevated and that failure to meet such standards could have serious consequences.

vocabulary.definition: Safety refers to the condition of being protected from or unlikely to cause danger, risk, or injury, particularly in the context of products, services, or environments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, safety is a critical consideration in product design, workplace environments, and regulatory compliance, often influencing consumer trust and brand reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: The concept of safety can vary across industries, with some sectors requiring stringent safety standards while others may prioritize innovation over safety considerations.

text: At Amazon, I was the first PM and then I drove the team around it for a no-code application development platform called Honey Code. So that was a brand new service. Amazon had never delved in that space before.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny asks for a specific example of disrupting yourself before competitors do, which Shweta had mentioned as an important lesson for large companies. Shweta shares how she led Amazon's first no-code application development platform called Honey Code, which was completely new territory for Amazon since they had previously focused on infrastructure services. This exemplifies her philosophy that established companies must innovate in new areas before startups disrupt them.
text_ko: 아마존에서 저는 첫 번째 프로덕트 매니저(Product Manager, PM)이었고, 허니코드(Honey Code)라는 노코드(no-code) 애플리케이션 개발 플랫폼을 위해 팀을 이끌었어요. 완전히 새로운 서비스였고 아마존은 그 분야에 이전에 진출한 적이 없었어요.
text_zh: 在亚马逊，我是第一个产品经理（PM），随后负责带团队推进一个叫 Honey Code 的无代码应用开发平台（no-code application development platform）。那完全是个全新的服务，亚马逊以前从来没涉足过这块儿。
text_es: En Amazon fui el primer gerente de producto (PM) y luego lideré al equipo para crear una plataforma de desarrollo de aplicaciones sin código (no-code) llamada Honey Code. Era un servicio totalmente nuevo: Amazon nunca se había adentrado en ese terreno.
key_sentence: I drove the team around it for a first of its kind service.
original_text: At Amazon, I was the first PM and then I drove the team around it for a no-code application development platform called Honey Code. So that was a brand new service. Amazon had never delved in that space before. It was more infrastructure focused and this was first of its kind service that the team worked on. And this has played out many times in my career, and so I am a big believer in disrupting yourself before somebody else does it.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating software applications, which includes planning, designing, coding, testing, and deploying software for various platforms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, application development is crucial for delivering products that meet user needs and drive business objectives, often involving agile methodologies.
vocabulary.nuance: While it generally refers to software, it can also encompass mobile and web applications, highlighting the importance of user experience.

vocabulary.definition: To investigate or research deeply into a subject or area of interest.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, delving into a topic often refers to thorough market research or analysis to uncover insights that inform strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a commitment to understanding complexities and nuances, making it suitable for academic or professional discussions.

vocabulary.definition: An intangible product offered to customers, which can include support, maintenance, or any form of assistance that meets a need.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of tech companies, a service often refers to software as a service (SaaS) models, where users access applications via the internet rather than through local installations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply varying levels of customer interaction and support, making it essential to specify the type of service being discussed.

text: I think a lot of that for me came by just being in different kind of situations and different kind of environments. And I think a lot of that for me came by just being in different kind of situations and different kind of environments.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny asks Shweta what helped her most develop listening and empathy skills, which she identified as underrated PM skills. Shweta explains that these crucial soft skills can only be developed through repeated practice across diverse work environments. She emphasizes that working with different types of teams, from startups to large companies, helped her understand various perspectives and constraints that different stakeholders face.
text_ko: 저한테는 그런 부분들이 다양한 상황과 환경에 직접 있어 보면서 많이 생긴 것 같아요. 다시 말하면, 여러 상황과 환경을 직접 겪으면서 그런 것들이 더 많이 생겼던 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得这主要是因为我接触了各种不同的情况和环境，在不同的场合都待过。我觉得这主要是因为我接触了各种不同的情况和环境，在不同的场合都待过。
text_es: Creo que gran parte de eso lo aprendí simplemente por estar en todo tipo de situaciones y ambientes diferentes. Y creo que gran parte de eso lo aprendí simplemente por estar en todo tipo de situaciones y ambientes diferentes.
key_sentence: being in different kind of situations and different kind of environments.

vocabulary.definition: Circumstances or conditions in which events occur or people find themselves, often influencing behavior and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding various situations is essential for risk management, strategic planning, and adapting to market changes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a range of contexts, from everyday occurrences to complex challenges, and is often used to emphasize the variability of experiences.

vocabulary.definition: The surrounding conditions, influences, or settings in which individuals or organizations operate, affecting behavior and performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, environments can refer to workplace culture, market conditions, or technological landscapes, all of which impact organizational success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can connote both physical spaces and abstract conditions, such as emotional or social environments, and is often used to highlight the importance of adaptability.

text: Are you proactively trying to challenge your own assumptions is extremely important, right? As a big enough product manager as well as a seasoned product leader, if you're not doing enough of that, then I think you might not be listening.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny and Shweta are discussing how to develop better listening skills as a product manager. Shweta offers a specific technique for improving listening abilities: actively questioning your own assumptions. She argues that experienced product managers should expect disagreement and debate - if everyone always agrees with you, it's likely because you're not truly listening to different perspectives or you're missing important viewpoints.
text_ko: 자신의 가정에 대해 스스로 적극적으로 의심하고 도전해 보는 건 정말 중요해요, 그렇죠? 영향력이 큰 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)이자 경험 많은 프로덕트 리더(product leader)라면, 그걸 충분히 하지 않는 건 아마도 다른 사람들 얘기를 제대로 듣지 않는 것일 수도 있다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 主动去质疑自己的假设非常重要，对吧？作为一个称职的产品经理 (product manager) 和资深的产品负责人 (product leader)，如果你不常这么做，我觉得你可能没在认真听取别人的反馈。
text_es: Que cuestiones de forma proactiva tus propias suposiciones es fundamental, ¿no? Si eres un gerente de producto (product manager) de cierto nivel, o un líder de producto (product leader) con experiencia, y no lo haces lo suficiente, creo que quizá no estés escuchando.
key_sentence: Proactively trying to challenge your own assumptions is extremely important.
original_text: Are you proactively trying to challenge your own assumptions is extremely important, right? As a big enough product manager as well as a seasoned product leader, if you're not doing enough of that, then I think you might not be listening. If there's no conflict, if there's no contention, then something is missing.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that anticipates and addresses potential issues before they arise, rather than reacting to them after they occur.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being proactive is essential for strategic planning and risk management, allowing leaders to seize opportunities and mitigate challenges effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: Proactively implies a sense of initiative and foresight, and is often used to encourage a forward-thinking approach rather than a passive one.

vocabulary.definition: To question or dispute the validity of something, often to provoke thought or encourage improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, challenging assumptions or processes is crucial for innovation and continuous improvement, as it fosters a culture of critical thinking.
vocabulary.nuance: Challenge can carry a connotation of confrontation, so it is important to frame it constructively to avoid defensiveness.

vocabulary.definition: Beliefs or statements taken for granted without proof, often serving as the foundation for further reasoning or decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, assumptions can significantly influence strategies and outcomes, making it vital to regularly evaluate and validate them to avoid missteps.
vocabulary.nuance: Assumptions can be implicit or explicit; recognizing and challenging them is essential for effective problem-solving and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: The active process of receiving and interpreting spoken messages, which involves not just hearing but also understanding and responding appropriately.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective listening is critical in business for fostering collaboration, understanding client needs, and enhancing team dynamics, as it promotes open communication.
vocabulary.nuance: Listening implies a deeper engagement than simply hearing; it suggests attentiveness and a willingness to consider others' perspectives.

text: I'm going to say something that might sound a little cheeky, but I think the way to get promoted is to not want it too badly. It is about you have to focus on the impact.
speaker: Shweta Shrivastava
context: Lenny asks Shweta for advice on getting promoted, given her experience being promoted many times and now promoting others. Shweta offers counterintuitive advice: don't focus too heavily on wanting the promotion itself. Instead, she suggests focusing on creating meaningful business impact and doing what's right for the company. She acknowledges this might sound contradictory since ambition is natural, but argues that obsessing over promotion can actually hurt your chances.
text_ko: 좀 건방지게 들릴 수도 있는데요, 제 생각엔 승진을 너무 간절히 바라지 않는 게 오히려 승진에 도움이 되는 방법이에요. 핵심은 임팩트(impact)에 집중하는 거예요.
text_zh: 我可能说得有点直接，但我觉得想升职最好的办法就是别太渴望它。关键是把精力放在你能带来的实际影响（impact）上。
text_es: Voy a decir algo que puede sonar un poco atrevido: creo que la forma de conseguir un ascenso es no desearlo con demasiadas ganas. Lo importante es que te enfoques en el impacto.
key_sentence: it is about you have to focus on the impact.
original_text: I'm going to say something that might sound a little cheeky, but I think the way to get promoted is to not want it too badly. It is about you have to focus on the impact. It's about having an impact and then doing what is right for the business. So not sort of optimizing things for your promotion, which look, we are all ambitious human beings.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that one thing has on another; a significant change or consequence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, measuring the impact of a project or initiative is crucial for assessing its effectiveness and guiding future decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'impact' can imply a positive effect, it can also refer to negative consequences, so context is important when using this term.

vocabulary.definition: The center of interest or activity; the concentration of attention or effort on a particular task or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, maintaining focus on key priorities is essential for achieving strategic goals and maximizing productivity.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'focus' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a narrow perspective that may overlook broader opportunities if not balanced appropriately.

vocabulary.definition: To be raised to a higher position or rank within an organization, often accompanied by increased responsibilities and compensation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, being promoted is typically seen as a recognition of an employee's contributions and potential for leadership, impacting morale and career trajectories.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry different implications depending on the context; for example, it may suggest merit-based advancement or, conversely, favoritism in some cases.
